title: Light/Dark theme option and mirroring system setting
body:
Hello,

I am using Light system theme during the day (since it "energizes" me more) and then dark system theme during the evening and night (since it saves my eyes and helps with winding down). OS automatically toggles between them depending on the time of the day. 

Right now most of my apps follow this by default or with small help (like f-person/auto-dark-mode.nvim for nvim and little lua snippet for wezterm). 

I was wondering if there is already working solution for this with Zellij?
Either by default config (ie. akin to how Zed does it [1]), plugin oraz 3rd party solution?

[1] 
```ts
"theme": {
  "mode": "light" | "dark" | "system",
  "dark": "One Dark",
  "light": "One Light"
},

```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I was thinking about something like that: 

https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/pull/3293 

Idea was following:
1. Introducing new config options: `theme_dark`, `theme_light`
2. During client startup we detect current system theme and see if corresponding `theme_dark/theme_light` is set - if yes we create palette based on theme set in `theme_dark/theme_light` variable - if no we fallback to `theme` or use `"default"` if even `theme` is not set. (already works)
3. In client we poll and check if system theme changed and if so we send message to server to resync client_attributes with new palette set (still WIP)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
IMO, config live-reload is enough to allow people script this in any OS/distribution.

I would rather prefer to setup mac/linux to run a script  (when switching dark<->light mode) that updates the current theme in my config.kdl than have the zellij server to constantly poll for system theme changes.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
If its a helpful datapoint, I would prefer not to have multiple config files for zellij, with one per theme. Instead, I think having the concept of multiple themes defined in the config makes more sense. You can then in your config file designate one as the default dark mode theme, one as the default light mode theme, and then configure whether the light mode is dark, light, or automatic by default. 

You can also have a command to control the mode, to enable people to script this. But I do think that automatic should be one of the options to use for modes, for those of us who just want a good all in one system without additional scripting.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
To address this feature gap, I change the theme in the config whenever I switch between light or dark modes like so:

```fish
function _change_zellij_theme -a THEME
        set -Ux ZELLIJ_CURRENT_THEME $THEME
        sed -i '' "s/^\(theme \)\(.*\)\$/\1\"$ZELLIJ_CURRENT_THEME\"/" $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/zellij/config.kdl
end
```

It works, because Zellij watches and reloads based on config changes. This function is used in my wider setup that monitors the OS’ light/dark settings.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
to add to @participant4's comment, live reloading was added in zellij 0.41.0:
https://zellij.dev/news/colliding-keybinds-plugin-manager/

I see there's also a new `reconfigure` plugin command:
https://zellij.dev/documentation/plugin-api-commands#reconfigure

would anyone be interested in a headless plugin that you can just send a msg through pipes to change the theme? like a headless plugin that's running in the background, then you could run something like this in scripts that run when switching between light/dark:
```
zellij pipe --plugin zj-theme -- gruvbox-dark
```

could also work with keybinds

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
I did this in gnome, it doesn't automatically change the theme, but it is something!

```bash
zz() {
  theme=$(gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme)
  if [[ $theme == *"prefer-dark"* ]]; then
    zellij options --theme gruvbox-dark
  else
    zellij options --theme gruvbox-light
  fi
}
```

one workaround not mentioned here so far is to use the "ansi" theme 

then the light/dark concern is lifted completely out of zellij, because it will use whatever colours are provided by the terminal emulator

then you can configure your terminal emulator to switch between light/dark as appropriate (assuming it has this feature)

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
Thanks @participant12! Quick question on usage after reading the release notes and trying it out.

Say my system is on light theme and my config is:

```
theme "catppuccin-frappe"
theme_dark "catppuccin-frappe"
theme_light "catppuccin-latte"
```

When I open a new zellij instance, it starts with catppuccin-frappe (`theme`), a dark theme.

Would it be possible to automatically choose the theme matching the system - `theme_light` in this example?

I wonder if `theme` could be ignored when `theme_dark`/`theme_light` are set.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body: Also, not to pile on, but another observation: when I change the system theme after opening zellij, the "startup tips" modal doesn't react to the theme change. I need to nudge it to force a redraw, e.g. by cycling through the tips with the arrow keys. Both of these issues can be worked around by setting `theme` to the system theme I use most often.
